title: Journal v2: schema-validated events, replay digest, and a per-work-item run index
summary: The journal stops being a loose JSONL buffer and becomes a versioned, schema-checked event log. `journal.rs` is split into five modules: `event.rs` (the envelope, actor/cost/evidence types, and ten payload types), `hash.rs` (the chain hash plus a new replay digest over decision fields only), `schema.rs` (a compiled JSON Schema validator run on every append), `index.rs` (a locked, atomically-written per-work-item run index), and `reader.rs` (a full chain-verifying replay). The on-disk location moves from `<state>/buffer/<run>.jsonl` to `<state>/runs/<run>.jsonl`, run ids are validated as safe path components, and a run-complete event now seals the chain. Callers in `checkpoint.rs` and `review_run.rs` move to the new `Actor` type; CI and the integration tests follow the directory rename.

lanes.label: Callers
lanes.subtitle: osf CLI commands that write events

nodes.label: Checkpoint runner
nodes.subtitle: osf verify --checkpoint
nodes.summary: Runs the checkpoint's moon tasks and writes one verification event per task plus a checkpoint-complete event. Now builds an `Actor::system("osf")` and fills the new `check_type` and `summary` fields with `None`.

nodes.label: Review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run::reduce_with
nodes.summary: Writes one review-answer event per judged attempt and one review-decision event for the whole review. Switched from a bare `&str` actor to `Actor::system(ACTOR)`.

nodes.label: Journal writer
nodes.subtitle: Journal::append / append_draft
nodes.summary: Computes the chain hash, validates the serialised event against the schema, records the run in the work-item index on the first accepted event, then appends one JSON line. A refused event writes no byte and leaves the head unchanged; a run-complete event seals the journal.

nodes.label: Event model
nodes.subtitle: event.rs
nodes.summary: The envelope (`Event`, `Change`, `Actor`, `Cost`) and ten payload types: run-started, verification, review, finding, state-change, run-complete, attention, checkpoint-complete, review-answer, review-decision. `EventDraft` is what a caller supplies; the journal fills in run, prev_hash and hash.

nodes.label: Hash chain
nodes.subtitle: hash.rs
nodes.summary: `event_hash` over prev_hash, the canonical JSON of payload/work_item/change/actor/cost, and nothing else. Adds `ReplayDigest`, a second SHA-256 over decision lines only, which drops timings, cache, cost, run ids and transcripts.

nodes.label: Schema validator
nodes.subtitle: schema.rs
nodes.summary: Compiles `event.schema.json` once into a `OnceLock<jsonschema::Validator>` and returns one reason string per problem, each naming the JSON path. Called by the writer before any line is written.

nodes.label: Run index
nodes.subtitle: index.rs
nodes.summary: One JSON file per work item under `<state>/index`, named by the SHA-256 of the work-item id, listing that item's run ids in recorded order. Writes go through a temp file renamed over the target, under an `fs4` advisory lock with a ten-second wait.

nodes.label: Journal reader
nodes.subtitle: reader.rs
nodes.summary: Reads a run back, checking every line against the schema, every prev_hash link, every recomputed hash, the run id, and that nothing follows run-complete. Returns a `RunJournal` with events, head hash, replay digest and a complete flag, or a typed `ReadError` and no partial list.

nodes.label: runs/<run>.jsonl
nodes.subtitle: was buffer/<run>.jsonl
nodes.summary: The per-run hash-chained event log. The directory was renamed from `buffer` to `runs`; the file format is still one JSON event per line with a trailing newline.

nodes.label: index/<sha256>.json
nodes.subtitle: per work item
nodes.summary: A work item's run list, plus a sibling `.lock` file that is never deleted. Created only when a journal carries a work item; a journal without one leaves no index directory behind.

nodes.label: event.schema.json
nodes.subtitle: draft 2020-12
nodes.summary: The event contract: required envelope fields, the ten event types, per-type payload shapes, and the conditional rules (a harness actor must name a model; a blocked state change must carry a cause and no other state may; only observed findings may name a verifier).

nodes.label: Decision 0005
nodes.subtitle: the factory domain model
nodes.summary: Amended to add the `system` actor kind, to name the review-answer and review-decision event types, and to say the replay digest rather than the chain head is what proves a replay.

nodes.label: CI checkpoint job
nodes.subtitle: .github/workflows/ci.yml
nodes.summary: The checkpoint-evidence artifact path follows the directory rename from `$OSF_STATE_DIR/buffer` to `$OSF_STATE_DIR/runs`.

edges.label: append(actor, payload)
edges.summary: The checkpoint runner's verification and checkpoint-complete events now go through the validating writer with an `Actor::system` value.

edges.label: append(actor, payload)
edges.summary: Review answers and the review decision are appended with `Actor::system(ACTOR)`.

edges.label: validate(event)
edges.summary: Every event is serialised to a `serde_json::Value` and checked against the compiled schema before a byte is written; the reasons are joined into the refusal message.

edges.label: event_hash(HashInput)
edges.summary: The chain hash is computed from the draft's payload, actor, cost, work item and change, plus the current head.

edges.label: record_run(work_item, run)
edges.summary: On the first accepted event of a run that carries a work item, the run is recorded in that item's index before the journal line lands; a failed index update refuses the event.

edges.label: one JSON line
edges.summary: The accepted event is appended as one line with a trailing newline, and the in-memory head advances to its hash.

edges.label: temp file renamed over target
edges.summary: The index body is written to a unique temporary sibling and renamed into place under an advisory lock, so a reader never sees a half-written index.

edges.label: read_to_string
edges.summary: The reader loads the run's file and checks it line by line; a missing file is `NotFound`, not an empty journal.

edges.label: validate(line)
edges.summary: Each line is checked against the same schema the writer used, so a hand-edited line that still hashes correctly is still refused.

edges.label: event_hash + ReplayDigest
edges.summary: The reader recomputes each event's chain hash and mixes its decision line into the replay digest, so a tampered payload breaks the chain at its own line.

edges.label: serde shape matches schema
edges.summary: The Rust types and the JSON Schema describe the same envelope; the schema is the contract the writer and reader both enforce.

edges.label: actor kinds, event types, replay
edges.summary: The amended decision is what the new `system` actor kind, the review-answer and review-decision types, and the replay digest implement.

edges.label: artifact upload
edges.summary: The CI job uploads the renamed directory as checkpoint evidence.

flows.title: Appending one journal event
flows.summary: What happens between a caller handing over a payload and a line landing on disk: hash, validate, index, write, seal.

messages.label: append(actor, timestamp, payload)
messages.note: The caller supplies an `Actor` and a payload; the journal owns the run, the previous hash and the hash.

messages.label: event_hash(prev_hash, payload, actor, cost, work_item, change)
messages.note: The chain hash covers the payload, actor, cost, work item and change, but not the run id or the timestamp.

messages.label: validate(event)
messages.note: A run-complete event whose head_hash is not the journal's current head is refused here too, alongside the schema reasons.

messages.label: record_run(work_item, run)
messages.note: Only on the first accepted event of a run that carries a work item; a failure here refuses the event before any line is written.

messages.label: one JSON line + newline
messages.note: The head advances only after the write succeeds.

messages.label: run_complete = true
messages.note: After a run-complete event is accepted, every later append is refused with 'the run is already complete'.

views.summary: The callers, the five journal modules, the two state directories they touch, and the schema and decision that govern them.
